newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-PAKISTAN TAKE FIRST INNINGS LEAD OVER NEW ZEALAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN TAKE FIRST INNINGS LEAD OVER NEW ZEALAND.

text.p: Moin Khan made a fighting half- century as Pakistan held an eight-run first innings lead over New Zealand at lunch on the second day of the first cricket test on Friday.
Moin scored a resolute 59 as Pakistan staged a fine recovery and went into the interval on 163 for eight in reply to New Zealand's first innings total of 155.
He shared a sixth-wicket stand of 48 with his overnight partner Salim Malik after Pakistan had resumed at 52 for five.
Malik, 11 overnight , went at 85 for 21 when Bryan Young took an overhead catch at second slip which gave paceman Simon Doull his fifth wicket of the innings.
Moin also dominated the seventh-wicket partnership of 56 in 18 overs with Saqlain Mushtaq which took the score to 141.

The Pakistani wicket-keeper brought up his fourth half-century with his ninth four, driving off-spinner Dipak Patel toward mid-wicket. He was eventually trapped leg before the wicket by seamer Justin Vaughan, who also had Waqar Younis lbw for two.
Saqlain was then joined by Mushtaq Ahmad and the pair pushed the score past New Zealand's total, having added 20 runs in an undefeated ninth-wicket stand.
At the interval, Saqlain was on 23 and Mushtaq 10. Doull's figure of five for 46 from 16 overs represented his career best. Vaughan has taken two for 16.
